title: Trend following
text: Trend following buys what has been rising and sells what has been falling, across dozens of futures markets at once. It is the core strategy of many CTAs, the commodity trading advisors who manage futures money for others.

title: Time series momentum
text: Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen gave it a precise form in 2012, in the Journal of Financial Economics, and called it time series momentum. They tested 58 liquid futures: equity indices, currencies, commodities and bonds. The rule looks only at each instrument's own past. If its return over the last twelve months is positive, be long for the next month. If it is negative, be short. Returns persisted for one to twelve months, and partly reversed over longer horizons.

title: Sizing by volatility
text: Sizing matters as much as direction. Each position is scaled to the same risk: 40 percent annualized volatility, divided by the instrument's own recent volatility. That volatility is an exponentially weighted average of squared daily returns, with a centre of mass of 60 days. So a future running at 20 percent volatility gets twice its notional, and one at 80 percent gets half. A calm bond and a wild commodity end up carrying similar risk.

title: Edge and risk
text: Why would trends persist at all? The authors call the pattern consistent with initial under-reaction to news, and delayed over-reaction. The strategy harvests those slow moves. It loses in choppy markets, where each false breakout is bought, then sold at a worse price. Sharp reversals hurt, because the signal always looks backwards. And volatility sizing means a quiet market that suddenly wakes up meets an oversized position.

title: In the lab
text: The lab's TrendFollower is the simplest version: a 20-day and a 50-day moving average of the close. It is long while the fast average is above the slow one, and short while it is below, sized at one million dollars. On QQQ's real daily closes in 2019, it started the year short, then flipped direction five times. QQQ rose from about 155 to 213 that year, yet the strategy lost about 20 thousand dollars, with a drawdown near 200 thousand. The whipsaws in May and August did the damage.

title: What it needs
text: The infrastructure is about breadth, not microseconds. You need clean continuous futures prices for many markets, with contract rolls handled. Execution rolls positions before expiry, and trades large size without moving the price much. Margin and cash have to be managed, because futures are leveraged. And risk is targeted across the portfolio, so one crowded theme cannot dominate.

title: Takeaway
text: Trend following harvests slow, persistent moves across many markets. It pays for them in whipsaws and sharp reversals, so diversification and volatility sizing do most of the work.
